projects.title: Real-Time Sleep Stage Detection Algorithm
projects.shortDescription: Real-time classification of sleep stages using machine learning.
projects.fullDescription: Nightly sleep patterns play an important role in the clinical evaluation of sleep quality. These patterns are characterised by distinct sleep stages identifiable from EEG recordings. Sleep stages (Awake, N1, N2, N3, REM) are traditionally classified manually by sleep technicians. While accurate, the process is time-consuming. In response, the project aimed to develop an AI-based sleep stage classifier that can automate and expedite this classification process. The workflow included EEG artefact removal, feature extraction and machine-learning model development.

projects.title: Statistical Inference for Ising Model
projects.shortDescription: Inferring Ising model parameters from simulated and neural spike data
projects.fullDescription: This project investigated the inverse Ising problem by inferring model parameters directly from observed spin data. Starting with the equilibrium case, simulated datasets were generated using the Metropolis algorithm and model parameters were recovered through gradient descent. The approach was then extended to non-equilibrium systems using Glauber dynamics and applied to both simulated data and real neural spike train recordings from salamander retinal ganglion cells. Model performance was assessed using log-likelihood and temporal correlation metrics.

projects.title: Molecular Dynamics
projects.shortDescription: Molecular dynamics simulation of a Lennard–Jones fluid
projects.fullDescription: This project simulated atomic interactions using a Lennard–Jones fluid model. Particle positions and velocities were evolved using the Verlet algorithm, with periodic boundary conditions applied to reduce finite-size effects. After the system reached equilibrium, key physical observables were computed through ensemble averaging, including thermodynamic quantities, spatial correlation functions and diffusion coefficients.

projects.title: Data Analysis for discovering the Higgs Bosons
projects.shortDescription: A simplified Higgs boson search using blind analysis to avoid bias in signal optimisation.
projects.fullDescription:
The Higgs boson is one of the fundamental particles associated with the quantum excitation of the Higgs field. The Higgs boson was not discovered until the ATLAS and CMS experiments at the Large Hadron Collider in 2012. 

 This project implemented a simplified Higgs boson search using blind analysis to avoid bias in signal optimisation. The analysis selected regions with the strongest signal while avoiding over-optimisation to rare statistical fluctuations.

projects.title: Quantum Circuits
projects.shortDescription: Quantum circuit simulations of confinement in the quantum Ising model
projects.fullDescription: This project studied confinement in the quantum Ising model by simulating real-time dynamics using a quantum circuit emulator. The system evolved under transverse and longitudinal magnetic fields, with its time evolution computed using the Suzuki–Trotter method. Magnetisation and spin–spin correlations were analysed to identify signatures of confinement and assess the feasibility of simulating many-body quantum dynamics.

projects.title: Transport and Traffic Simulation
projects.shortDescription: An agent-based model demonstrating how traffic jams emerge from local vehicle interactions
projects.fullDescription: This project explored traffic flow using agent-based modelling to explain the emergence of congestion without accidents or traffic signals, known as phantom traffic jams. Individual vehicles were modelled as agents that respond only to nearby cars, yet collective traffic patterns such as stop-and-go waves emerge from these local interactions. The simulation displayed how complex system-level behaviour can arise from simple rules.

projects.title: Bacterical Colony Counting
projects.shortDescription: Computer vision analysis of bacterial persister dynamics from microscopy images
projects.fullDescription:
This project investigated the dynamics of bacterial persister cells, specifically intracellular Klebsiella pneumoniae under antibiotic treatment. In addition to experimental measurements, the project emphasised computational image analysis to extract quantitative insights from microscopy data. 

 Computer vision techniques were developed to automatically process time-lapse images, enabling the detection, tracking and quantification of bacterial colonies over time. This automated analysis was used to estimate wake-up rates and growth dynamics.

projects.title: Compton Scattering
projects.shortDescription: Experimental measurements and Monte Carlo simulations of Compton scattering
projects.fullDescription: This project studied Compton scattering using both experimental measurements and computational simulations. Photon energies scattered at different angles from a Cs-137 source were measured and compared with Monte Carlo simulations modelling photon scattering in two dimensions.

projects.title: Angular Analysis of Particle Decay
projects.shortDescription: Angular analysis of B-meson decays using LHCb data to test Standard Model predictions
projects.fullDescription:
The Standard Model (SM) is a framework to understand the behaviour of fundamental particles and their interactions through EM, weak and strong forces. In particle physics research, scientists test the predictions of the SM against experimental observations to ensure its consistency. Any deviations from expected patterns in these observations may indicate the presence of phenomena beyond the SM. 

 This project focused on the study of B-meson decays using a large dataset collected by the LHCb experiment. The aim was to analyse the coefficients of a specific angular distribution to identify potential deviations from SM predictions. The analysis involved background subtraction, acceptance corrections, fitting the data to the angular distribution, quantifying uncertainties and comparing the results with theoretical expectations.

projects.title: Underwater Search and Rescue Strategies
projects.shortDescription: Bayesian inference for underwater search and rescue strategies
projects.fullDescription: This was my final-year bachelor’s project, aiming to explore strategies for underwater search and rescue operations using Bayesian inference as a core approach. The project evaluated the effectiveness of Bayesian search methods and compared their performance with random search approaches.

projects.title: Thermodynamics: Snookered Systems
projects.shortDescription: An OOP-based simulation of gas dynamics
projects.fullDescription: A simulation of gas behaviour, which enabledx real-time visualisation of molecular dynamics and verification of the ideal gas law and Boltzmann distribution.

projects.title: Active Particle Simulations for Lithium-Ion Batteries
projects.fullDescription:
Battery research has become increasingly important in addressing global energy and sustainability challenges. The growing demand for portable electronics, electric vehicles, and renewable energy storage systems highlights the need for efficient, durable and cost-effective battery technologies. 

 This study focused on computational modelling to improve battery performance. ABAQUS, an engineering software, was used to simulate the mechanical behaviour of battery cathodes, which required the generation of active particles (APs) to represent the microstructure. 

 I specifically contributed to automating the creation of APs in ABAQUS for a high-volume fraction polymer matrix in lithium-ion batteries. The involved developing Python scripts to algorithmically generate coordinates for the APs, which significantly streamlined the simulation workflow.
